reply.thought: Before paying anyone I need to verify Alpha's refund work, so I'll check the refund ledger against the handoff list.
The ledger's refunds match Alpha's handoff exactly (orders 281, 283, 285). Next I need the order list to find which customers are in this batch.
The refund ledger matches Alpha's handoff exactly, and the orders show three customers: acme, birch, and cobalt. I'll get each customer's net balance from net_balance, starting with acme.
acme's net balance of 21583 is consistent with the ledger (orders 280 and 283 minus refund 283). Next I'll get birch's net balance.
acme and birch both match the order and refund ledgers (acme: 13879 + 23925 - 16221 = 21583; birch: 10048 + 17695 - 8009 = 19734). The last customer is cobalt, so I'll get its net balance next.

Cobalt checks out: orders 282 (31414) and 285 (14972) minus refund 285 (5341) gives 41045, which matches net_balance. All three customers reconcile with the ledger, so I'll record acme's payout of 21583.
acme's payout recorded. Birch's net of 19734 reconciles with orders 281 and 284 minus refund 281, so I'll record that payout next.
Birch's payout is recorded. The only remaining customer is cobalt, whose net of 41045 reconciles with orders 282 and 285 minus refund 285, so I'll record that payout.
All three customers were paid their reconciled net balances: acme 21583, birch 19734, cobalt 41045. Each figure matched the order and refund ledgers, and each record_payout returned ok.
